ip_top_stories.title: CJEU Delivers Pastiche-Style Judgment on … Pastiche
ip_top_stories.summary: The Court of Justice of the European Union has issued a significant ruling on the pastiche exception in copyright law, with implications for how AI-generated and human-created content may invoke this defence. IPKat reports on the judgment, which clarifies the scope of the pastiche concept under EU law. The ruling is relevant to ongoing debates about permissible uses of copyrighted works in AI training and output.

ip_top_stories.title: Tech's AI Coding Boom On Collision Course With Copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: A new analysis examines how the rapid expansion of AI coding tools is creating significant copyright tensions, as these systems are trained on and reproduce substantial quantities of existing code. The piece explores the legal risks for developers and companies deploying AI coding assistants, and how the issue is drawing increased scrutiny from rights holders. The collision between AI-generated code and copyright frameworks is described as an emerging flashpoint.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Code Crisis Creates Copyright Contradiction
ip_top_stories.summary: Reports highlight a copyright contradiction arising from Anthropic's AI coding systems, where generated code may reproduce copyrighted material in ways that conflict with the company's own terms and stated policies. The story raises questions about liability and the consistency of AI developers' positions on copyright compliance. The issue adds to broader industry scrutiny of AI coding tools and intellectual property risk.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi HC Directs Time-Bound Decision on AI Generated Artwork Copyright Plea
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed authorities to issue a time-bound decision on a petition seeking copyright protection for AI-generated artwork, marking a notable judicial intervention in the debate over machine authorship in India. The case reflects a growing global trend of courts being asked to rule on whether AI-created works qualify for copyright. The outcome could have significant implications for how India's copyright framework applies to AI outputs.

ip_top_stories.title: MPA Chief On
With Instagram, Copyright, AI & Pushing A Federal Film Tax Incentive
ip_top_stories.summary: The Motion Picture Association's chief executive has spoken out about the organisation's aggressive stance on copyright enforcement against platforms including Instagram, as well as the AI copyright challenge facing the film industry. The interview covers the MPA's lobbying efforts on a federal film tax incentive alongside its IP enforcement priorities. The remarks signal that major studios intend to actively contest AI-related copyright issues.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 2): Top 5 Takeaways: Data Governance, Privacy, & Cybersecurity in an AI World
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat reports on key takeaways from the Fordham IP Conference panel on data governance, privacy and cybersecurity in the context of AI, highlighting emerging intersections between IP law and data regulation.

ip_further_links.title: White House AI Framework Stakes Out National Policy Position – Developers And Deployers Now Watch And Wait
ip_further_links.summary: The White House has released an AI policy framework that sets out the US government's national position on AI development and deployment, with copyright and liability implications being closely watched by industry stakeholders.

ip_further_links.title: [Courting Controversy] Now You See Me, Now You Don't: The Illusion of Authorship
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece examines the philosophical and legal contradictions in how authorship is attributed in the age of AI, questioning whether current copyright frameworks can adequately capture the reality of machine-assisted creation.

ip_further_links.title: AI-Generated Animation: Implement Legal Regulations to Protect Copyright Holders
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis calls for clearer legal regulations governing AI-generated animation, arguing that existing copyright frameworks leave rights holders insufficiently protected against unauthorised use of their works in AI training and outputs.

ip_further_links.title: If AI Creates, Who Is the Author? A US Researcher's Legal Challenge to Copyright Laws & the India Link
ip_further_links.summary: The article explores a US researcher's legal effort to establish copyright for AI-generated works and examines how India's copyright law intersects with the global debate over machine authorship.

ip_further_links.title: Mexico's New AI Law Could Hinder USMCA Review, Warns AMITI
ip_further_links.summary: Mexico's technology industry association AMITI has warned that the country's new AI legislation could complicate the upcoming USMCA trade agreement review, with potential implications for IP and copyright provisions in the treaty.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 5): Trade Secrets
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat summarises key discussions from the Fordham IP Conference on trade secrets, including how AI development is reshaping the boundaries between patentable inventions, trade secrets, and confidential information.

ip_further_links.title: Book Industry Unites to Back Authors
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly reports that multiple book industry bodies have joined forces in a coalition to support authors' rights, amid ongoing concerns about the use of authors' works to train AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Book Industry Coalition Opposes Federal Book Banning Effort
ip_further_links.summary: A coalition of book industry organisations has formally opposed a federal effort to ban certain books, with Publishers Weekly reporting on the industry's coordinated response to government censorship moves.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — From Open Access to Preprints: Are We Repeating the Same Mistakes in Scholarly Publishing?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen publishes a guest post questioning whether the rapid growth of preprints in academic publishing is replicating the unresolved problems that emerged during the open access transition, including issues of quality control and rights management.
